card.title: Electric Charges and Charging by Induction

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Electric charge is a fundamental, quantized ($q = ne$), and conserved property of matter. Objects can be charged by triboelectric friction, conduction, or electrostatic induction. Charging by induction polarizes mobile electrons in an insulated conductor; momentary grounding allows electron exchange with Earth, permanently trapping an opposite net charge on the conductor without losing inducing charge.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Quantization of electric charge: $q = \pm n e \quad (n \in \mathbb{Z}^+)$
Conservation of electric charge: $\sum q_{\text{initial}} = \sum q_{\text{final}}$
Charge sharing between identical conducting spheres in contact: $q' = \frac{q_1 + q_2}{2}$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Thinking induction creates new charge: Induction does not generate charge from nothing; it redistributes existing mobile valence electrons within the conductor while preserving net charge conservation of the combined system.  ·  Believing grounding always pulls electrons down to Earth: If a positively charged rod is inducing negative charge near it, grounding pulls electrons UP from the Earth into the conductor. If a negative rod is near, electrons flow DOWN into the Earth.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Grounding must be removed BEFORE withdrawing the inducing charged body; otherwise, mobile charges equalize back through ground, leaving the sphere neutral.  ·  Repulsion is the only sure test of electrification because an uncharged body can be attracted by a charged body due to electrostatic polarization.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Electrostatic precipitators: Industrial smoke stacks ionize airborne fly ash and soot particles, which are attracted to grounded collecting plates, purifying factory exhaust by over 99%.  ·  Photocopier (Xerography): An aluminum drum coated with photoconductive selenium is charged by corona wire in the dark; light from the document discharges illuminated areas, leaving an electrostatic latent image that attracts toner powder.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Assuming insulators can be charged permanently by induction: Only materials with delocalized mobile charges (conductors) can be charged by induction and grounding. Insulators experience only molecular dielectric polarization.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Draw sequential schematic diagrams showing charging a conductor by induction.  ·  Calculate electron deficiency or excess for a given charge magnitude.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Quantization check: divide given charge Q by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; if n is not an integer, the charge is physically impossible.  ·  Induction charge sign: Induced net charge on conductor is ALWAYS opposite to the sign of the inducing rod.

rows.text: Q1. State the fundamental law of electrostatics and discuss the three fundamental properties of electric charges.  ·  Q2. Explain the principle and step-by-step procedural sequence for charging an insulated metallic sphere negatively by induction.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Quantization and conservation of electric charge.  ·  Step-by-step mechanism of electrostatic induction and earthing.  ·  Origin of triboelectric series and conduction charge sharing.  ·  Gold-leaf electroscope working and repulsion as the sure test of electrification.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Electric charge is quantized in integral multiples of $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.  ·  Charge is an isolated invariant scalar conserved across all nuclear and electromagnetic interactions.  ·  Induction charges a conductor with the sign opposite to that of the inducing charged body without contact loss.  ·  Grounding neutralizes electrostatic potential by allowing electron exchange with Earth's infinite charge reservoir.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Charge is an absolute relativistic invariant: an electron's charge remains exactly $1.602176634 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$ whether at rest in a laboratory or traveling at $99.999\%$ the speed of light in the Large Hadron Collider.  ·  Quarks carry fractional charges ($+\frac{2}{3}e$ and $-\frac{1}{3}e$), but because of quantum chromodynamic color confinement, quarks never exist as isolated free particles; all observable free entities have integer charge multiples $ne$.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Q3. Can a body possess a net static charge of $4.0 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$? Justify your answer using the principle of charge quantization.  ·  Q4. A glass rod rubbed with silk attracts tiny bits of paper. Why does a piece of paper jump to the rod, touch it, and then vigorously fly away?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Electrostatic spray painting: Paint droplets are given a uniform negative charge as they leave the nozzle, while the metal car frame is grounded/positive. Mutual repulsion atomizes the spray into a fine mist that wraps uniformly around the car.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Electric Charge & Elementary Charge:** Electric charge is an intrinsic physical property of elementary matter that governs all electromagnetic interactions. Charges exist in two polarities designated by Benjamin Franklin as positive (carried by protons, $+e$) and negative (carried by electrons, $-e$).…  ·  **Quantization of Charge:** Electric charge is not continuous; it exists only in discrete integral multiples of the elementary electronic charge: $q = \pm n e$, where $n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. Quantization was first demonstrated macroscopically by Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909).…  ·  **Conservation & Additivity of Charge:** In any isolated thermodynamic system, the algebraic sum of all electric charges remains strictly constant regardless of physical or chemical transformations: $\sum q_{initial} = \sum q_{final}$.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fractional quark composition of nucleon: $p = uud \; (+1e), \quad n = udd \; (0)$  ·  Electrostatic attraction occurs between unlike charges and between any charged body and a neutral conductor via polarization.  ·  Remember that in conductors, only negative charges (free conduction electrons) physically move; positive ionic cores remain fixed in the crystal lattice.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 1: Electric charge is quantized, meaning it exists only in integral multiples of the fundamental charge e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.  ·  Statement 2: The total electric charge of an isolated system remains constant over time regardless of physical or chemical reactions.  ·  Statement 3: Electrostatic induction allows charging a conductor with a sign opposite to that of the inducing charged object without physical contact.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 4: Repulsion is the definitive test of electrification, since neutral matter is attracted to any charged body by polarization.  ·  Statement 5: Charge is invariant under relativistic transformations, independent of the relative velocity of the frame of reference.  ·  Identical spheres contact trick: Touching identical spheres of charges q₁ and q₂ redistributes charge equally to (q₁ + q₂)/2 each.
